beats.heading: My week at Humanitarians AI
beats.narration_text: This week at Humanitarians AI, I focused on educational video reviews, YouTube publishing materials, and four Claude Bear videos about Claude Skills. My work involved content from Anjana, Tanmay, and Onkar. This is Liam, narrating for Deepa. I reviewed and prepared publishing materials; I did not create the four Claude Bear videos.

beats.heading: Reviewing team submissions
beats.narration_text: I reviewed submissions from Anjana, Tanmay, and Onkar for educational content, presentation quality, and suitability for YouTube. I checked clarity, organization, visual presentation, and whether viewers could follow the explanation. I also worked on titles and descriptions, and identified items that might need clarification before publication.

beats.heading: A finished file still needs review
beats.narration_text: This helped me understand why educational quality control matters. A technically complete video still needs evaluation for readability, consistency, and audience engagement. Reviewing different contributors’ work also showed me the importance of consistent publishing standards. Technical completion is a starting point, not a complete judgment of educational value.

beats.heading: Claude Web Artifacts Builder
beats.narration_text: For Web Artifacts Builder, I prepared a YouTube title and structured description covering the skill’s purpose, workflow, benefits, and limitations. I included a hands-on activity, topic information, and relevant hashtags. I learned that an AI-built interface does not automatically guarantee code quality, accessibility, or a good user experience.

beats.heading: Claude Webapp Testing
beats.narration_text: For Webapp Testing, I prepared the title, description, and viewer exercise. I focused on automated testing, functionality, user interactions, and validating results. My lesson was that tests can identify problems efficiently, but a passing result does not guarantee a completely defect-free application. The choice of test cases still matters.

beats.heading: Claude XLSX
beats.narration_text: For XLSX, I reviewed publishing readiness and prepared a title and description. I checked format and presentation, identified visuals worth verifying, and explained pandas, openpyxl, formulas, and validation. I learned that spreadsheet automation reduces repetitive work, but formula correctness and business accuracy are different. Human verification remains important.

beats.heading: Claude Slack GIF Creator
beats.narration_text: For Slack GIF Creator, I prepared a title and description about animation workflows, technical requirements, creative limitations, and a viewer exercise. I learned that generating an animation successfully does not guarantee effective communication. Timing, readability, context, and audience interpretation all matter when judging the result.

beats.heading: Organizing publishing materials
beats.narration_text: I organized publishing materials using a consistent format: an introduction, explanation of the skill, practical application, limitations, and a hands-on activity. The Claude Bear materials included descriptive titles, educational summaries, hashtags, and viewer exercises. This connected technical details with a clear purpose for the audience.

beats.heading: Confirm the playlist
beats.narration_text: I contacted Sanjana to clarify the playlist for the Claude Bear submissions. Claude Basics was my proposed category, while I sought confirmation before finalizing it. I learned to confirm publishing requirements rather than assume them. This report does not claim playlist approval or that all videos were published.

beats.heading: What I am taking forward
beats.narration_text: My takeaways were stronger video-review and quality-assurance skills, experience writing structured publishing materials, and a better understanding of four Claude Skills and their limitations. I also practiced team coordination. The common lesson was to distinguish useful AI automation from the human judgment needed to assess an educational outcome.
